title: Maximize the Number of Target Nodes After Connecting Trees II
summary: Given two trees with n and m nodes, represented by their edges, determine the maximum number of nodes in the first tree that can be targets for each node, by connecting one node from the first tree to any node in the second tree.
statement: Given two trees with n and m nodes, represented by their edges, determine the maximum number of nodes in the first tree that can be targets for each node, by connecting one node from the first tree to any node in the second tree. The target condition is met if the path length is even, including the node itself. Each query is independent, and the added edge is removed before the next query.
constraints: Each edge list describes a separate labeled tree with at least two nodes.
For each first-tree node independently, add one temporary edge between any nodes of the two trees.
A target has even path distance from the source; maximize the target count for every first-tree source.
hints: Every tree is bipartite, and two nodes have even distance exactly when their colors match.
Count the two color classes in each tree; bridge endpoints can select the larger second-tree class.
Two-color both trees; for each first node add its own color-class size and max(second color sizes).
The bridge flips parity once, while choosing its endpoints lets either second-tree color class become even-distance targets.
editorial: The bridge flips parity once, while choosing its endpoints lets either second-tree color class become even-distance targets.

tests.explanation: Tree bipartitions give the five optimized totals 8, 7, 7, 8, and 8.
Each source has one even-distance node in its own tree and can gain one from the other tree.
